title: Annual boiler service by a licensed heating tech
why: A steam boiler needs a yearly combustion and safety check before the heating season. Book early; October fills up.
how: Call a licensed heating tech (about 15 min to book, 1 to 2 hr visit). Ask for: combustion test, low-water cut-off and pressuretrol check, flue inspection, and a look at the near-boiler piping. Log the visit in the steam log as "service".
safety: Licensed pro only. Do not do this yourself. Gas, burner and flue work is for a licensed tech.

title: Radiator valves and pitch walk-through
why: One-pipe steam only works if each radiator slopes slightly back toward its single supply valve so condensate drains out, and the valve is fully open or fully closed. A half-open valve causes banging and spitting.
how: About 1 hr, system cold. Put a level on each radiator: it should tilt slightly toward the valve. Check that every supply valve is fully open (or fully closed on a room you are not heating). Look for weeping at the valve packing nut. Note problem radiators.
safety: System must be cold and off. Do not open or close valves on a hot system.

title: Test radiator air vents
why: Each radiator vent lets air out so steam can fill the radiator. A stuck or spitting vent gives cold radiators or water spray. Vents wear out in a few years.
how: About 30 min, system cold. Take each vent off and blow through it: it should pass air freely and be closed when hot. Replace vents that are clogged, stuck, or leaking. Note the model and size on each radiator.
safety: System must be cold and off. Hot vents burn.

title: Inspect main vents on the steam mains
why: Main vents let air out of the big steam pipes so steam reaches the far radiators quickly. A failed main vent means slow heat and wasted fuel.
how: About 30 min, system cold. Find each main vent near the end of a steam main. Look for corrosion, leaks and clogs. Replace failed vents (they commonly last 10 to 20 years). Venting capacity should suit the length of the main; ask your tech if unsure.
safety: System must be cold and off.

title: Set boiler water level before the first heat
why: The boiler should start the season at the proper water level or it can shut down on low water or be damaged.
how: About 10 min, boiler cold. The water in the gauge glass should sit in the range your boiler manual marks, commonly about halfway. If low, add water slowly through the fill valve or auto-feed as your manual says. Note unusual color.
safety: Never add cold water to a hot boiler that has run low. Turn it off and call a licensed pro.

title: Check boiler water level
why: A boiler that runs low can be damaged or lock out. Checking weekly in the heating season catches leaks and feed problems early.
how: About 2 min. Look at the gauge glass: the level should be steady in the normal range. A level that keeps dropping means a leak or a feed problem; log it in the steam log and call your tech.
safety: If the glass is empty or no water shows, turn the boiler off and call a licensed pro.

title: Low-water cut-off blow-down (follow your manual)
why: The low-water cut-off stops the burner if water gets low. Sediment can make it stick, so makers call for a periodic blow-down in the heating season. The interval depends on the model: many say monthly, some weekly.
how: About 10 min. Follow the procedure printed in YOUR low-water cut-off or boiler manual, and use the interval it gives (change this task's schedule to match). If you have never done it, ask your tech to show you at the annual service. Log it in the steam log as "blowdown".
safety: Scalding hot water and steam. Do not guess the procedure; use the manual or have your licensed tech do it.

title: Check boiler pressure gauge and pressuretrol
why: Home steam systems run on ounces, not pounds. Typical settings are a cut-out around 1 to 2 psi. Higher pressure wastes fuel and strains old piping.
how: About 15 min. While the boiler runs, watch the pressure gauge: it should stay well under 2 psi. If it goes higher, log it and ask your tech to lower the settings.
safety: Adjusting controls is for a licensed tech or someone trained on your boiler.

title: Listen for water hammer and cold radiators
why: Banging or cold radiators point to pitch, vent or pipe-drain problems you can fix early.
how: About 15 min while the system is heating. Note each radiator that bangs, spits or stays cold. Usual causes: radiator not pitched to the valve, stuck vent, half-open valve, or a low spot in a pipe holding water.
safety: Do not touch hot pipes or valves.

title: Skim or flush boiler water, only if it looks dirty
why: Dirty water makes the boiler surge and send out wet steam.
how: Only if the water in the glass looks brown or foamy, or the level bounces. Follow the skimming steps in your boiler manual, or have your tech do it at the annual service.
safety: Hot water and steam hazard. Use the manual or a licensed pro.

title: Look for drips and rust around the boiler and basement piping
why: Small drips at fittings and valves turn into big repairs and keep the boiler topping up with fresh, mineral-rich water.
how: About 15 min with a flashlight. Look at joints, valves and the pipes near the boiler for wet spots, white crust or rust. Photograph anything new. Repairs to boiler piping are for a licensed pro.
safety: Do not tighten or repair boiler fittings yourself. Licensed pro.

title: Look at old pipe and boiler insulation (do not touch)
why: Houses this age often have old white or gray wrap on steam pipes or the boiler that may contain asbestos. It is only a risk when damaged and disturbed.
how: About 10 min, look only. If the wrap is torn, flaking or crumbling, keep people away, do not sweep or vacuum it, and call a licensed asbestos pro for testing and repair. Intact wrap that is left alone is usually fine.
safety: Licensed pro only. Do not do this yourself. Suspected asbestos: do not disturb it or try to test it yourself.

title: End-of-season boiler layup
why: Some techs recommend a final check and leaving the boiler filled to the right level over summer to limit corrosion.
how: About 30 min. Follow your tech's layup instructions or the boiler manual. Write down any problems (noises, cold radiators, leaks) for the service call.
safety: Gas shutoff or burner work is licensed pro only.

title: Test smoke and CO alarms
why: A monthly press-the-button test confirms the alarm works. Heating season is when carbon monoxide risk rises.
how: About 5 min. Press the test button on every smoke and CO alarm. If one is silent or chirps, replace the battery.

title: Replace alarm batteries and check alarm ages
why: Massachusetts law requires working smoke and CO alarms. Alarms wear out: check the date on the back and replace the unit if it is past the date printed on it (commonly 10 years for smoke, 5 to 10 for CO).
how: About 30 min. Fresh batteries in every unit; replace any expired alarm. Write install dates in Assets.

title: Check fire extinguishers
why: An extinguisher with low pressure does nothing.
how: About 10 min. Gauge needle in the green, pin and seal intact, no dents or rust. Replace or have it serviced if not.

title: Test GFCI outlets and breakers
why: GFCI outlets protect you near water; they can fail without notice.
how: About 10 min. Press TEST then RESET on each GFCI outlet (kitchen, baths, garage, outdoors, basement). If TEST does not cut power, replace the outlet; call a licensed electrician if you are not experienced.
safety: Any panel or wiring work: licensed electrician.

title: Look at the electrical panel (cover stays on)
why: Rust, scorch marks, a buzzing sound or a warm panel are warning signs.
how: About 5 min, look only. Do not open the panel cover. If anything looks or smells wrong, leave it alone and call a licensed electrician. Keep the area in front of the panel clear.
safety: Licensed pro only. Do not do this yourself. Main electrical work is licensed electrician only.

title: Chimney and flue inspection
why: Blocked or cracked flues cause carbon monoxide and fire risk.
how: About 1 hr visit. Have a chimney professional inspect and sweep, and check the boiler flue connection. Keep the report in Documents.
safety: Licensed pro only. Do not do this yourself. Flue work is licensed pro only.

title: Exercise main water shutoff and fixture shutoffs
why: Old valves seize if never moved; you want them to work the day you need them.
how: About 15 min. Turn the main water shutoff off and on gently, and each sink and toilet stop valve a quarter turn. If a valve leaks or will not move, do not force it; call a plumber. Make sure everyone knows where the main is (see Shutoffs).

title: Review what to do if you smell gas
why: Gas leaks need a fast, correct response.
how: About 5 min. Rehearse it: leave the house right away, do not touch switches or phones inside, call the gas company or 911 from outside. Put the utility emergency number on the fridge.
safety: Licensed pro only. Do not do this yourself. Never look for a gas leak yourself.

title: Winterize outdoor faucets
why: Frozen hose bibs split pipes behind the wall. Do this before the first hard freeze (late October to early November in Massachusetts).
how: About 30 min. Remove hoses. Close the interior shutoff for each bib, open the outdoor spigot to drain and leave it open. Add insulated covers. Frost-free bibs still need hoses off.

title: Clean gutters after leaf drop
why: Clogged gutters cause ice dams and wet foundations.
how: About 2 to 3 hr with a ladder, gloves, hose and scoop. Clear debris, flush downspouts, make sure water leaves 4 to 6 ft from the foundation.
safety: Ladder safety. Stay off the roof. Hire it out if you are not comfortable on a ladder.

title: Storm windows and weatherstripping
why: Drafts in an old house add up. Less heat loss means the boiler runs less.
how: About 2 to 4 hr. Hang storm windows, seal gaps with rope caulk or weatherstripping, check door sweeps.
safety: Pre-1978 windows and trim may have lead paint. Do not sand or scrape it dry; licensed pro if paint will be disturbed.

title: Replace range hood and humidifier filters (if you have them)
why: Clean filters keep air and airflow healthy. Steam heat has no furnace filter.
how: About 30 min. Swap the filters you have. Track the exact sizes and next due dates under Consumables.

title: Clean dryer vent
why: Lint buildup is a leading cause of house fires.
how: About 45 min. Disconnect the duct, brush its full length, vacuum, reconnect with foil tape (not screws).
safety: Unplug the dryer. Gas dryer: any gas line work is licensed pro only.

title: Flush water heater and test relief valve
why: Sediment shortens the life of a tank water heater.
how: About 1 hr with a hose and bucket. Follow the manual for the flush. Lift the relief (T and P) valve lever briefly only if the manual says to; it can stick open afterward.
safety: Hot water. For a gas or oil heater, gas, burner and flue work is licensed pro only.

title: Check tub and shower caulk and spout
why: Failed caulk leaks into walls.
how: About 15 min. Inspect caulk and the tub spout joint; recaulk where it is cracked or lifting.

title: Check washing machine hoses
why: Rubber hoses burst. Braided steel hoses last longer.
how: About 10 min. Look for bulges, cracks or rust at the fittings. Replace rubber hoses every 5 years or so. Turn the supply valves off when you go away.

title: Review warranties and documents that expire soon
why: File claims before coverage lapses.
how: About 15 min. Open Assets and Documents and look for anything expiring in the next 90 days.

title: Cold snap preparation
why: Below about 10 F, pipes in exterior walls and cold basements can freeze.
how: About 20 min. Know where your main water shutoff is, locate pipes in exterior walls, and plan to open cabinet doors under sinks on those walls and let a faucet drip when a hard freeze is forecast. Keep the basement heated.

title: Watch for ice dams after heavy snow
why: Ice dams force water under shingles and into ceilings and walls.
how: About 15 min after a big snow. Use a roof rake to clear the first 3 to 4 ft from the ground. Check ceilings and upper walls for stains. The long-term fix is air sealing and attic insulation.
safety: Never climb an icy roof or ladder. Hire a pro for ice removal.

title: Check indoor humidity and window condensation
why: Very dry air or condensation on old windows signals a moisture balance problem.
how: About 5 min with a hygrometer. Aim for about 30 to 40 percent in winter. Adjust a humidifier if you use one.

title: Test sump pump (if you have one)
why: Spring snowmelt and rain are peak sump season.
how: About 15 min. Pour water into the pit until the float lifts the pump. Confirm it discharges and the check valve works. Clean the inlet screen.
safety: Unplug before touching the pump.

title: Inspect roof and flashing from the ground
why: Winter damage shows up as lifted shingles or failed flashing.
how: About 30 min with binoculars. Look for missing or curled shingles, chimney flashing and gutter sag. Photograph problems.
safety: Stay off the roof.

title: Exterior walk-around: siding, paint, caulk, foundation
why: Catch rot and gaps early.
how: About 1 hr. Probe wood trim with a screwdriver, note paint failures, check foundation cracks and window caulk. Photograph and date anything new.
safety: Paint on a pre-1978 house may contain lead. Do not dry-sand or scrape it. Disturbing it: licensed pro (lead-safe certified).

title: Check gutters and downspouts in spring
why: Winter ice can pull gutters loose.
how: About 30 min. Look for sagging, loose hangers and clogs; run a hose to confirm the flow.
safety: Ladder safety.

title: Window AC and fan prep
why: Clean units cool better and use less power.
how: About 30 min. Clean filters and coils before installing.
safety: Unplug before cleaning.

title: Check grading and downspout discharge
why: Water near the foundation is the top cause of wet basements.
how: About 20 min. Run a hose or watch a rain: water should flow away from the house.

title: Basement moisture check
why: Humid summers drive mold in basements.
how: About 15 min with a hygrometer. Keep it below about 60 percent. Run a dehumidifier and empty it or plumb a drain.

title: Look in the attic for leaks and pests
why: Roof leaks and nests are easy to fix when small.
how: About 20 min on a dry day with a flashlight. Look for stains, daylight, droppings, damp insulation. Do not disturb old insulation if it could be vermiculite; suspected asbestos is a licensed pro job.
safety: Suspected asbestos: licensed pro. Watch your footing on the joists.

title: Check trees for dead or hanging limbs
why: Winter storms leave limbs that can fall on the house or cars.
how: About 20 min from the ground. Look for dead limbs near the house, roof and wires. Call a licensed arborist for anything large or near power lines.
safety: Stay away from wires. Large limbs: licensed arborist.

title: Fall yard cleanup and bring in hoses and furniture
why: Leaves against the foundation hold moisture, and hoses left out freeze and crack.
how: About 1 to 2 hr. Rake leaves away from the foundation, drain and store hoses, put away outdoor furniture.
